01 — The Problem
Scorelines hide the quality of chances

THE FIX
xG reframes the result

Measure opportunity quality, not only whether the ball went in. A 35-meter strike is not equivalent to a six-yard tap-in.

02 — The Object
xG is a probability, not a verdict
WHAT THE MODEL ESTIMATES
xG = P(Y = 1 | x)

Conditional probability

Estimate whether a shot outcome Y equals 1 given feature vector x.

02

Bounded domain

Every shot receives a value strictly between 0.00 and 1.00.

03

Team total

One shot receives a likelihood. A team total adds those likelihoods across individual shots.

03 — Geometry
Distance is the first geometric signal

Pitch grid: model shot location on a standard 105m × 68m coordinate projection.

Probability decay: goal likelihood drops sharply beyond roughly 16 meters.

d = √((xs − xg)² + (ys − yg)²)

(xs, ys) shot · (xg, yg) goal centre

xG FOR A CENTRAL SHOT VS DISTANCE · DRAG ALONG THE CURVE d 16.0 m → xG 0.00
04 — Target Window
Visible goal angle captures the target window
GOAL WIDTH

The standard separation between posts is w = 7.32m.

LAW OF COSINES · LIVE
cos θ = (a² + b² − w²) / 2ab
= …

a and b are distances to the posts; w is goal width. Drag the shooter.

INTERPRETATION

A wider unblocked angle generally means more target area. PSxG: Post-Shot xG evaluates shot-placement precision and goalkeeper shot-stopping ability.

05 — Context
Location is only the start

Features that change conversion probability. Toggle them on a fixed shot from the penalty spot.

SAME SPOT · NEW CONTEXT
0.27base

z = −1.02

Effects are illustrative log-odds shifts. Each feature adds context to location. Expected Threat (xT) uses Markov decision chains to map ball progression across an N × M grid.

Geometry describes the window. Context describes the shot.

06 — The Link Function
Logistic regression turns features into probability

Log-odds linearity: combine engineered features into an unbounded score z.

Sigmoid transformation: compress z monotonically into a valid probability range.

p = σ(z) = 1 / (1 + e−z)
z = β0 + β⊤x
SLIDE THE SCORE z z = 0.00 → p = 0.50
07 — Training
Training punishes confident mistakes
01 · MAXIMUM LIKELIHOOD
L(β) = Σi [yi log pi + (1 − yi) log(1 − pi)]

Maximize the joint probability of observed outcomes; yi is the result, pi its predicted probability.

02 · BINARY CROSS-ENTROPY

A confident wrong prediction receives a severe penalty.

03 · CONVEX CONVERGENCE

Gradient descent can reach a global optimum for the logistic objective.

PREDICTED xG p · DRAG TO SEE THE PENALTYp = 0.90
■ if it went in (y=1): loss 0.11
■ if it missed (y=0): loss 2.30
